profile.headline: Undergraduate Researcher at Carnegie Mellon University
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary: Currently looking for interesting software projects to work on.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Implemented a location clustering service allowing healthcare professionals to more easily publish listings on major websites

Developed an Uber-link redirect service that directs consumers to target businesses in the Uber app

Designed and Implemented a high-availability API gateway that delivers location data to thousands of business pages at once

Streamlined the process of adding filters to the location search page, saving over 20 man-hours per week

Maintained and improved the location search server’s back-end

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
Conducted research on the effectiveness of using authentication based on spatial recognition for smartphones

Developed an app for Google Android in which the user can create paths going through a world of dynamically generated rooms, and attempt to recreate these paths

Incorporated the path-matching ability of the above app into a multi-tiered authentication system that guards access to various resources within an Android phone

positions.title: 15-251 Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Covered topics such as combinatorics, graph theory, probability, number theory, finite automata, computability, and complexity

Led weekly recitations and held several office hours for students each week

Wrote up and graded problems sets and exams

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Designed and implemented a Python library that automates server management tasks for the Chrome OS hardware testing lab

Consolidated logs of server management tasks into a single, easily accessible location

Improved the work flow of the server management team by saving over 20 man-hours per week

positions.title: Lead Developer
positions.description:
Led full stack development of a fantasy sports startup that was funded by Microsoft Ventures.

Built a Node.js server interfacing with a highly scalable database in Cassandra that can handle thousands of concurrent users

Created a site in which users can enter contests to guess and wager on fantasy values of athletes.

educations.degreeName: Bachelor's of Science in Computer Science

honors.title: 1st Place in the 2015 Algorithms with a Purpose Competition
honors.issuer: Issued by Carnegie Mellon University's Association for Computing Machinery · Nov 2015

honors.title: CMU Tartanhacks - Bloomberg Best Hack
honors.description: Hacked a Predictive Financial Tool which takes in random sets of data and allows users to buy/sell the data from a day to day basis.
